summary: Regression test for WhatsApp URL normalization fix (bug: wa link 404'd due to messy phones with '+', spaces, hyphens producing 'api.whatsapp.com/resolve/?deeplink=...%2520' style URLs). Verified across ALL 4 frontend consumers (Home CTA, ProductDetail chat, AdminInvoices send, Checkout) plus backend /api/whatsapp/build with 5 messy-phone variants. 100% pass — every generated URL is a canonical https://wa.me/{digits-only-phone}?text={single-encoded} link with no %2520, no %250A, no api.whatsapp.com/resolve.

issues: Footer displays 'Wa: ++62 882-8936-6448' (double '+') when settings.whatsapp_number itself already begins with '+'. The footer text seems to prepend a '+' unconditionally. The actual wa.me link ([data-testid=home-wa-cta]) is correct (normalized). Only the DISPLAY string is doubled. Cosmetic, not the bug being tested.

action_items: Optional cosmetic: In Home.jsx footer, don't prepend '+' to settings.whatsapp_number for display — either strip existing '+' first, or better: use a display formatter that normalizes then re-adds a single '+'. This is a MINOR display-only bug; the wa.me link is unaffected.
critical_code_review_comments: backend/server.py normalize_phone() (~L1411) correctly strips all non-digits and handles Indonesian leading-0 -> 62 substitution. Uses urllib.parse.quote(msg, safe='') at L1450 for single-encoding — correct.

frontend/src/lib/api.js buildWhatsAppUrl() uses encodeURIComponent(message) exactly once and returns empty string when phone digits are missing — matches backend behavior. Guards against buildWhatsAppUrl with empty phone in all 4 consumers (early return + toast). Good.

All 4 consumers (Home.jsx, ProductDetail.jsx, AdminInvoices.jsx, Checkout.jsx) migrated to the shared helpers as claimed. No stragglers using api.whatsapp.com/resolve pattern remain. grep for 'api.whatsapp.com/resolve' returns zero hits in frontend/src.
Checkout flow correctly uses SETTINGS.whatsapp_number (STORE's WA) via server-side /whatsapp/build — customer's messy phone is only echoed in the message body, not used as target.
